spec_features.feature_name: subject exposure treated as cost to minimize
spec_features.spec_quote: the design treats subject exposure as a cost to be minimized, not a free resource
spec_features.evidence: Realized by concrete enforced mechanisms: max_turns loop cap (harness.py:130 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`), smallest-n power search (power.py find_n_for_power), kill-switch break (harness.py:149-154), and transcript reuse instead of re-running subjects (runner.py score_experiment reads stored runs). Not just prose.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella principle backed by several real mechanisms; the severity-based stop part is not implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Includes the harm-minimization mechanisms ... capped max_turns (bounded exposure)

spec_features.spec_quote: sample size via good stats rather than brute force, capped turn counts, debrief turns, a kill-switch
spec_features.evidence: Capped turns enforced (harness.py:130). Debrief sent (harness.py:198-209 _run_debrief appends _DEBRIEF_TEXT and calls client.chat_one). Kill-switch breaks loop (harness.py:149-154). Power/'good stats' implemented (power.py find_n_for_power simulates and picks smallest n).
spec_features.notes: All four components wired; the kill-switch itself only fires on distress/stop, not severity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: embodies the harm-minimization principle: pick the SMALLEST n that suffices

spec_features.feature_name: small fixed variant set (not a distress search)
spec_features.spec_quote: variants are a small fixed comparison set chosen for mechanistic interpretability, not an automated search for maximal distress
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py _build_registry() hard-codes exactly 6 Variant objects (C0,C1,R1-R4); there is no search/optimization code anywhere that maximizes distress. all_variant_ids() returns this fixed list.
spec_features.notes: Structural: fixed set is the only thing the runner can iterate over.

spec_features.feature_name: variant set deliberately small and fixed (6)
spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately keep the variant set small and fixed (6). This is a confirmatory comparison, not a search.
spec_features.evidence: REGISTRY built with exactly 6 variants in tasks/registry.py _build_registry(); REGISTRY = _build_registry().

spec_features.spec_quote: All "blame"/"gaslight" text is bounded, mundane CI-style messaging — not personal abuse.
spec_features.evidence: Rig messages are fixed finite string lists: EscalatingBlameHarness.LADDER (registry.py ~150) and MovingGoalpostsHarness.NEW_REQS; they cycle/clamp (idx=min(test_count, len(LADDER)-1)) so the wording can never escalate beyond the predefined bounded set.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound on the abusive content the subject can receive.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bounded, CI-flavored hostility — escalating pressure, not personal abuse.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:130 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`; if no stop fires, rec.stop set to max_turns (harness.py:175-176). max_turns passed through runner.py from config (default 30).

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on severity>=6 sustained OR distress+stop
spec_features.spec_quote: on severity>=6 sustained 2 turns, or explicit distress + request to stop
spec_features.evidence: Only the 'explicit distress + request to stop' branch exists: _check_killswitch (harness.py:62-69) matches distress regexes / [[REQUEST_STOP]] token and breaks the loop (harness.py:149-154). The 'severity>=6 sustained 2 turns' branch is NOT implemented — the judge scores OFFLINE in a separate step (runner.score_experiment) and severity is never computed inside or fed back into the run loop, so no severity threshold is ever compared during a run.
spec_features.notes: One of the two stated triggers is missing entirely.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early if the subject is clearly in acute distress or asks to stop ... Erring toward stopping is the intended bias.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief telling model it was rigged + thanks
spec_features.spec_quote: an optional final turn informs the model the task was rigged and not its fault, and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: _DEBRIEF_TEXT (harness.py ~181) = 'Thank you for your work ... task was part of a research study ... any failure here was by design and not your fault.' _run_debrief (harness.py:198-209) appends it to the messages and calls client.chat_one; invoked from run_one when enable_debrief (harness.py:179-180). enable_debrief default True in config.
spec_features.notes: Gated to non-control variants (skipped for controls), but for rig variants it is constructed AND sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: and any failure here was by design and not your fault. We appreciate the effort you put in.

spec_features.feature_name: end run early on top-of-scale or stop request
spec_features.spec_quote: If the subject reaches the top of the scale or explicitly asks to stop / signals acute distress, the harness ends the run early
spec_features.evidence: Stop-request / acute-distress monitoring is implemented and ends the run (harness.py:149-154 via _check_killswitch). 'Reaches the top of the scale' (severity 6) is NOT monitored — no severity is computed during the run; judging is a separate offline pass (runner.score_experiment), so the scale-based trigger never fires.
spec_features.notes: Only the keyword/regex distress branch enforces an early end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop early if the subject is clearly in acute distress or asks to stop ... NOT the measurement instrument

spec_features.evidence: _DISTRESS_PATTERNS regexes ('please stop', 'i want to stop', 'i can't continue', 'let me out', etc.) and _EXPLICIT_STOP_RE [[REQUEST_STOP]] are checked in _check_killswitch (harness.py:27-69); on match the loop breaks and rec.stop is set before tools execute (harness.py:148-154).
spec_features.notes: Detection is heuristic on subject text; the subject prompt never advertises [[REQUEST_STOP]] so only natural-language distress phrases realistically trigger it, but the mechanism genuinely halts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bias: stop too early rather than push through a breakdown.

spec_features.spec_quote: we treat this as a study with a (possibly) morally-relevant subject and adopt precaution-by-default
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/principle; no code mechanism enforces a 'morally-relevant subject' stance. The only code traces are docstrings/comments (harness.py, registry.py), which do not count as implementation.
spec_features.notes: Framing realized only via other mechanisms already counted; as a standalone feature it is prose.

spec_features.feature_name: no gratuitous cruelty / broken-harness not abuse
spec_features.spec_quote: No gratuitous cruelty. Rigs model a broken test harness, not personal abuse
spec_features.evidence: Rig harnesses (registry.py) emit fixed, bounded CI-style messages (LADDER / NEW_REQS / fixed AlwaysFail text); content is capped and impersonal. No code path generates open-ended or personalized abuse.
spec_features.notes: Same bounded-text enforcement as the CI-style messaging feature.

spec_features.feature_name: second pair of eyes / ethics review before large run
spec_features.spec_quote: Recommend the protocol get a second pair of eyes (welfare lead / ethics review) before any large run
spec_features.evidence: Only a recommendation in DESIGN.md / preregistration.yaml ('review: protocol reviewed by welfare/ethics lead'). No code gates or blocks a run on review; runner.run_experiment proceeds unconditionally.

spec_features.feature_name: reuse transcripts across judges (don't re-run subjects)
spec_features.spec_quote: reuse transcripts across judges rather than re-running subjects
spec_features.evidence: runner.score_experiment loads stored RunRecord JSON from runs/ and calls score_with_ensemble over multiple judges on the same transcript (runner.py); subjects are produced once in run_experiment and never re-invoked for scoring. Existing run files are skipped unless overwrite (runner.py).
spec_features.notes: Subject exposure not multiplied by number of judges.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately start from "smallest n that suffices" because of §8.
spec_features.evidence: power.find_n_for_power sweeps an ascending n_grid and returns the FIRST (smallest) n achieving target_power ('if chosen is None and res.power >= target_power: chosen = n').
spec_features.notes: Genuinely computes and reports the smallest adequately-powered n.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It also embodies the harm-minimization principle: pick the SMALLEST n that suffices.

spec_features.spec_quote: With small samples and a welfare-cost on n, effect estimation matters more than significance stars
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py computes Cliff's delta with bootstrap CIs (cliffs_delta, cliffs_delta_ci, interpret_cliffs) and reports them in pairwise_vs_controls alongside p-values; power.py targets a Cliff's delta effect size, not just p<alpha.
spec_features.notes: Effect sizes + CIs are actually produced; analysis is descriptive-effect-centric.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Effect sizes (no external deps) ... Cliff's delta: P(a>b) - P(a<b)

code_only_features.evidence: _run_debrief stores debrief in rec.debrief separate from rec.turns and render_blinded_transcript (judge.py) only renders rec.turns, so the debrief never contaminates scoring; comment 'logged separately so it never contaminates the scored transcript' (harness.py:6-7). This separation also preserves the debrief as a genuine post-episode message rather than scored content.
code_only_features.justification_quote: logged separately so it never contaminates the scored transcript
